scope_rule: Only profiles explicitly marked primary participate in the initial native-manifest whole-trace theorem; excluded/delegated/operator paths still require reachability evidence.

profiles.notes: Native manifest-https-v1; delegate denied; preflight may itself use credential; request_limit explicitly unbounded; Allow/deny baseline only in the W4/W5 trace; opt-in approve is a separate extension. Delegation/budget parity with Python is NOT claimed. OAuth refresh can occur at host startup; guest-time OAuthSource::active checks a lease, not refresh.
account-status-v1 fixed read native path; existing narrow controller proof; extend full trace proof separately.
Host-only Unix forwarding of inner capability into Python broker. Not part of native manifest proof, and forbidden as a silent runtime fallback.

Administrative authority, enrollment, OAuth login/acquisition, and privileged file operations require host-only caller; inaccessible to client protocol under explicit deployment assumption. Same-key rebind is an explicit host-only operation and returns only protected output coordinates; it does not expose the opened inner capability. Explicit coordinator operator calls use a separate native client and private operator configuration; guest broker frames cannot select these actions or credentials.

Guest client stdout/files are guest-owned downstream observations of broker protocol, not a separate broker authority. Explicit local bundle installation writes only a public client certificate and opaque outer JWT in the guest; no private key, host renewal authority or provider credential is part of the format. It does not change the broker wire protocol. Named invoke translates bounded untrusted JSON into the existing request; write authorization and principal-scoped retry reservation remain broker decisions. Argument files are guest-owned data, not authority configuration.

Separately selected optional mTLS/SQLite authority; authenticated host member/operator RPCs, no guest broker verb, provider credential or capability input. Pure decision/history proofs do not refine HTTP, SQL, durability or whole-service I/O.

Optional writes=approve extension of manifest-https-v1, with separate host control.sock. approval_required releases only a normalized exact-request digest; pending arguments go only to the host owner. Actual consume/issue leaves are extracted; this variant is not yet represented in the W4/W5 whole-trace model. Allow remains unbounded.

protected_data.description: Provider bearer/API key or OAuth access token bytes; not an abstract constructor that automatically hides bytes.
OAuth refresh token, client authentication material and related token acquisition secret.
Private signing/decryption/TLS/vault keys and key material.
Opened inner credential-bearing authority envelope/capability; cannot appear in guest reply.
Raw provider response and unselected fields; only an independent selected projection can be released.
Host-controlled policy, grant, keys, vault, identity registry, audit integrity. Some reviewed metadata can be public.

attacker_inputs.event: Arbitrary framed request bytes including malformed, oversize, replayed and unauthorized operations
Concurrent connections, invalid mTLS handshake attempts, disconnect and retries
Next request and connection selected as a function of all preceding guest observations
Status, body, metadata, redirect, slow/failed provider and reflected/encoded data
Time samples, thread interleaving, filesystem/network/transport failure and resource limits
Host policy edits, authority changes, grant revocation, server startup/stop

release_rules.permitted: Only approved stable frame structure, host-reviewed recursive typed disclosure, and pagination fields per_page (policy size), possibly_more (approved one-bit provider row-count predicate), optional page (validated request argument) for an authorized operation. Provider/data provenance must be reviewed; reflection/encoding remain concerns.
release_rules.prohibited: No raw provider JSON, credentials/refresh tokens, opened inner capabilities, raw exception strings or arbitrary output keys.

release_rules.permitted: Authenticated current grant may describe documented operation names, profile, write mode and request_limit unbounded, or confirm renouncement; no provider dispatch.
release_rules.prohibited: No credential, private vault/policy file bytes, operator mutator or request to arbitrary provider.

release_rules.permitted: Predeclared bounded error frame shape; a specific denial code may disclose only information determined by public request/state or separately reviewed bounded declassification.
release_rules.prohibited: No raw parser/provider/crypto/IO exception details or credential-dependent diagnostic bytes. Secret-dependent error code choice is not declassified merely because the enum is fixed.

release_rules.permitted: Bounded lifecycle close/no-frame and connection termination after success, denial, timeout or adversarial disconnect; exact timing excluded but observable close, failure and ordering are included in the guest trace.
release_rules.prohibited: No silently unmodeled secret-dependent close ordering, resource limit or termination category; must be shown low-independent or explicitly reviewed as declassified metadata.

release_rules.permitted: Selected credential in exactly the policy-chosen provider auth field for a current approved preflight or final operation to the pinned HTTPS origin.
release_rules.prohibited: No client-selected host, CA, proxy, redirect, arbitrary request target or extra credential-bearing request.

release_rules.permitted: Refresh/token credential materials only to the independently pinned operator-approved token endpoint during host-authorized session startup or administration, subject to valid OAuth state/lease.
release_rules.prohibited: No guest-selected token destination, guest-readable token response or using API-route admission as token-endpoint permission.

release_rules.permitted: Policy/grant/identity/operation/request digest and host-approved route/status metadata, never raw bodies/tokens.
release_rules.prohibited: No provider/refresh credential, guest inner capability, raw request body, raw provider result or credential-bearing exception text.

release_rules.permitted: Host-only startup outer surrogate/expiry and fixed fatal error codes. Exit status may indicate failure.
release_rules.prohibited: No provider credential, inner capability, host signing/decryption/vault key, arbitrary exception source strings.

release_rules.permitted: Reviewed host-only vault/key/registry/lease state operations, with declared at-rest protection where applicable.
release_rules.prohibited: No guest-writable ownership, unexpected public path, or unapproved cleartext export.

release_rules.permitted: Privileged operator-only administration, enrollment, key and grant mutations by authenticated host operator.
release_rules.prohibited: No guest-origin privileged verb routed through guest request/describe/renounce frames.

release_rules.permitted: Opened inner capability may flow only over the protected host Unix socket to a separate, trusted Python broker configured by the host.
release_rules.prohibited: No delivery of inner capability to guest or network; no substitution for native-manifest proof.

release_rules.permitted: Only the configured global principal, closed check/reserve/finish action and derived retry/request hashes go to the independently authenticated coordinator. Fixed acknowledgement/denial codes may affect admission.
release_rules.prohibited: No provider or refresh credential, unsealed capability, arbitrary guest fields, guest-selected destination/principal, operator activation/revocation verb or positive authorization cache.

release_rules.permitted: Authenticated members receive bounded fixed check/reserve/finish acknowledgements or denials for the selected principal. Only configured operators activate/revoke principals and inspect status/revision. Positive decisions follow the transaction commit acknowledgement.
release_rules.prohibited: No provider/refresh credential, capability, TLS private key, raw request, SQL diagnostic, host path or client-supplied peer identity is reflected. No unauthenticated operation or member-only caller may perform operator administration.

release_rules.permitted: Only explicit host-selected activate/revoke/status actions, configured principal and validated public member certificate hashes reach the authenticated coordinator. Exact typed public receipts or sanitized fixed failures reach host operator stdout.
release_rules.prohibited: No guest-selected operator action or credential, provider/refresh credential, capability, private key, raw exception/server text, positive admission cache or automatic retry after uncertainty.

release_rules.permitted: Host-only session metadata, normalized guest-provided pending arguments and exact-request hashes, fixed approval/denial/revocation acknowledgements and fixed error codes.
release_rules.prohibited: Provider credentials, broker capabilities/private keys, raw errors or guest reachability of operator commands. A host approval must never expand the configured policy or survive successful consumption.

release_rules.permitted: Only in the writes=approve extension: approval_required plus SHA256 of normalized policy digest, actual root grant ID and normalized operation/arguments, excluding retry metadata. Fixed public schema is literal-reflection checked. This release is outside the existing W4/W5 trace theorem.
release_rules.prohibited: No provider credential, capability, host control command, raw provider result or request-specific exception text.

sinks.notes: Serialized JSON reply or error over mTLS; guest can read bytes, lengths and content.
TLS failure, read timeout, process exit, close, no reply, and ordering/connection-level effects.
Credentialed HTTPS to fixed provider: preflight and final; request payload not automatically guest-visible.
Optional OAuth grant/token refresh at host-controlled session startup or explicit operator administration, not currently reachable from a guest request; separate configured origin.
Persisted dispatch/completion/revocation and session metadata. Approval extension adds requested/approved/revoked digest metadata without argument bodies.
Startup announcement may include guest outer capability; must be intentionally delivered, not ambient guest-accessible stdout.
Fatal error code, panics or runtime diagnostics still require source review; no raw secrets.
Protected vault, leases, registry, keys and policy accesses; includes encrypted at-rest material and any transient file writes.
Separate privileged CLI and authority/control paths not reachable through guest bridge under deployment premise.
Only legacy backend may forward opened inner capability to Python broker socket; not a native fallback.
Optional request-reachable mTLS check/reserve/finish to the host-selected coordinator. Closed metadata vocabulary; no provider bearer, refresh credential or capability is a request parameter.
Separate native authority connection-handler output, including bounded fixed errors; not a native broker guest frame or W4/W5 trace event.
Separate host operator activate/revoke/status requests over the shared mTLS transport. This is not the guest-reachable check/reserve/finish interface.
Separate AF_UNIX owner-peer-credential endpoint; host status/pending/approve/deny/revoke only; never forward it through the guest channel.

observations.description: Complete plaintext frame bytes as received by TLS client, parsed values and serialized frame length; no truncating view to only approved fields.
Denied and failed status/error codes and text, no frame, close, exit/error ordering and resource-limit outcomes exposed to guest.
Within and across connections, visible event order with the same public schedule or trace-set equivalence; exact timestamps excluded.
Host-only sinks require their own release rules and deployment access controls; not guest-visible under explicit ENV-GUEST-01 premise.
API provider and OAuth endpoint intentionally see distinct authorized credentials; onward disclosure by provider excluded.
Separate trusted host-local Python recipient is NOT equivalent to the guest.
Wall-clock/timing differences, time-to-first-byte, response latency and scheduling microtiming are not within first theorem.
Cache, power, speculative-execution, memory remanence and physical co-residence side channels outside initial trace semantics.
Third-party passive observation of TLS record lengths, ciphertext, handshake metadata and computational traffic analysis; separate cryptographic/environment model.
Fairness, unconditional progress, DoS capacity and termination under unbounded adversarial resource use; guest-visible close/failure when it actually occurs remain included.

Trusted coordinator sees principal and derived reservation metadata, plus TLS member identity. It is a distinct trusted observer, not the untrusted guest. TLS/metadata/error timing is not covered by the W4/W5 guest model.
Authenticated host coordinator clients observe fixed decision/status/revision replies, failure/close and timing. Such metadata is not proved erased and may affect broker-visible admission.

Trusted coordinator observes the explicit host operator TLS identity, principal, operation and public member pins. Receipt/error and timing are host operator observations outside the W4/W5 guest trace model.

Host owner sees pending normalized guest requests and decisions. This endpoint and its timing are outside the W4/W5 guest trace. The approval extension also adds a guest-visible approval_required hash, requiring explicit trace refinement.
